- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
---
title: "What an export includes"
description: "The rules every export shares: what it matches, what it waits for, how it treats missing media, graphics and captions, and what it labels."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Whichever format you pick, every export follows the same rules. This page says what ends up in the file, what an export stops to wait for, and what makes it fail.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Export…" keys="⌘E" tools="export" />

## The same picture and sound

An export uses the same composition and the same compositor as the preview, so what you see while editing is what the file holds. It always writes the whole timeline, or the [range](/export/range/) you pick, even with a [nest](/editing/nests/) open.

View-only settings never reach the file: [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/), [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/), [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/), [safe areas](/canvas/safe-areas/) and the [scopes](/color/scopes/).

The sound goes through a master limiter the preview doesn't have, so a mix that passes its ceiling sounds louder while editing than in the file. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).

## Waiting for what it needs

Some of what a file holds has to be made first. An export waits for all of it, and never writes that sound silent or that clip uncut. If it can't be made, the export fails and names the clip, except for a cursor track.

| It waits for | Which clips | If it can't be made |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Masks, made on this Mac | Every clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) that the export draws, in GIF and Animated PNG too | "Clip 4's person masks could not be made: …" (or "foreground masks", for a picture set to Foreground) and no file is written |
| [Rendered sound](/speed/ramp-audio/) | Every speed ramp, and every clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off | "Clip 4's retimed audio could not be rendered: …" |
| The isolated voice | Every clip with [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) | "Clip 4's isolated voice could not be rendered: …" |
| The voice effect | Every clip with a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) | "Clip 4's voice effect could not be rendered: …" |
| The clip's measured loudness and speech | Every clip with the [gate](/audio/gate/), [leveller](/audio/leveller/) or [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) on, because their thresholds follow it | See below |
| Cursor tracks | Every clip with a [recorded cursor](/recording/cursor/) | The clip draws without its cursor, the export goes on, and the finished line counts a cursor warning |

Only the loudness wait has a limit. If a measurement hasn't landed after five minutes, the export fails with "Clip 4's loudness or speech has not been measured yet, so its gate, leveller and de-esser cannot be set. Wait for their Status rows to show the clip's loudness, then export again." A clip that will never be measured, because it's silent or under 0.4 seconds, doesn't hold the export up and exports as the preview plays it.

While it waits, the [progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/) reads "Preparing “Board.mp4”…", and a row in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/#rows-and-their-states) stays at `Writing · 0 %`. You can cancel at any point. An Animated GIF or Animated PNG has no sound, so it waits only for masks and cursor tracks.

[Save Frame](/export/save-frame/#waiting-for-masks) works differently: it waits up to 30 seconds for masks, then saves the clip whole.

## Missing media

A clip whose file is missing still exports, showing its slate and with no sound. So does a [reversed clip](/speed/reverse/) whose backwards copy isn't rendered yet.

An audio track none of whose clips can be read is written as silence, rather than failing the export. To put the real footage back first, [relink the media](/projects/relink-media/).

## Graphics

An export draws the [graphics](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/) as they were when you asked for it, even if a module is saved again while it runs. That also keeps a [queued job](/export/export-queue/#a-queued-jobs-snapshot) stable.

If a graphic in the range doesn't compile or has no module, the export doesn't start: "The export was not started: the graphic "lower-third" … Fix the module and export again." This counts every graphic in a nest the range reaches, even one outside the part that plays. An audio-only export skips the check.

That check is only a compile, so a graphic can still fail part-way through. The export then stops at that frame, names the graphic and leaves no file: "The export was stopped at frame 120 of the graphic "lower-third": … No file was written."

## Captions

Captions are ordinary text clips, so they're always burned into the picture. They're never a subtitle track a viewer can switch off. To write a separate subtitle file, use [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/).

## Colour labels

An exported file carries colour labels, so players read it correctly. SDR files are labelled BT.709, and [HDR files](/hdr/export-hdr/) BT.2020 with HLG or PQ. A GIF carries no label.

- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)

3:description: "How a motion graphic works in Frame Job: a small module kept in your project that draws each frame, the clips it draws, and what its limits are."
9:A graphic is a motion graphic, such as a lower third, a chart or a countdown, drawn fresh on every frame by a small JavaScript module kept inside your project. You change what it shows with ordinary controls in the inspector, and you don't need to touch any code unless you want to.
26:Frame Job comes with 23 [ready-made graphics](/graphics/templates/). You can also bring in a module of your own, [write one](/graphics/write-a-module/), or have [an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) write one. To put one on the timeline, see [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
30:## Modules
32:A module is one file, `graphics/<name>.js`, in your project. It draws a picture, as SVG (a text format for vector drawings), for any frame Frame Job asks for.

3:description: Compress and limit a track's whole sound, or everything in a nest together, and know where the preview differs from the export.
68:## Exact in the export, approximate in the preview
72:The preview can only approximate this. Where a track's clips overlap, such as a crossfade or a nest's tracks, the preview plays the track's sound in more than one piece and runs the compressor and limiter on each piece separately. So the pieces can add up past a track limiter's ceiling while you edit, even though the export holds it.
74:While any track has a compressor or limiter and the preview plays at normal speed, the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) says so in its footer: "The mix as the preview plays it, with track compressors and limiters approximate, before the export's loudness and master limiter."
77:Judge a track limiter's ceiling on the export, not on the preview's meters.

69:H.264, HEVC and HEVC with Alpha are all 8-bit, so in an HDR project they write the project's SDR version and **Dynamic Range:** stays greyed out on **SDR version**. To deliver HDR in this family, use HEVC 10-bit.
